sources.entry: Synapse - Server for Matrix, an open standard for decentralized persistent communication. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Python/deb

summary.one_liner: Synapse is Element's open source reference implementation of a Matrix homeserver, the server side of the decentralized Matrix open standard for real-time communication.
summary.what_it_does: Synapse is a Matrix homeserver implementation written and maintained by Element. The README says it can be run and managed directly from this source code. It is licensed under AGPL, or under a paid commercial license from Element. The README points to documentation for standalone installation, configuration options, federation setup, reverse proxy use, and upgrades. It also describes developer resources such as the database schema, implementation notes, and a contributor guide. Element's Element Server Suite (ESS) is named as the official deployment method, available in Community, Pro, and TI-M editions.
use_cases: Hosting federated real-time chat for a community
Setting up a private messaging server for an organization
Placing a Matrix server behind a reverse proxy
how_to_run: See the Synapse documentation for standalone installation options
Recommended deployment method: Element Server Suite (ESS)
notable: Reference implementation of the Matrix homeserver
Dual-licensed: AGPL or paid Element commercial license
Official deployment shipped via Element Server Suite (ESS)
Supports federation with other Matrix servers
Documentation covers configuration, reverse proxy, and upgrades
caveats: Community support is only available through Matrix rooms; Element provides support only with an ESS subscription
GitHub issues are for bug reports and feature requests, not support
Commercial use outside AGPL terms requires a paid Element license
summary.license: AGPL-3.0 or commercial license from Element (dual-licensed)
